SMTO-SKL-0097 — The Microsoft 365 item changed before your edit was saved

GUID: 9503c146-1ac5-53dc-9f03-8cc076289070
Slug: microsoft365-precondition-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Someone or something changed this email, event, contact or file after it was last read. To avoid overwriting that newer change, your edit was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to read the item again, or open it in Outlook or OneDrive, and look at what changed. Your edit was based on an older version, so you need to see the newer changes first.
  2. If your change is still needed, ask the Agent to make it again on the current version. Once you've seen the latest version, it's safe to try the change again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the change as saved and the item shows it in Outlook or OneDrive.

If it still fails

  • If the item keeps changing, someone else may be editing it at the same time; agree with them who updates it. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 write was refused because the item's version (ETag) no longer matched: the pre-write read returned a different ETag than the one supplied, or Graph returned 412 / ErrorInvalidChangeKey.

What this means

  • Graph reports HTTP 412 or ErrorInvalidChangeKey, or pre-write readback differs from an explicitly supplied ETag. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph reports HTTP 412 or ErrorInvalidChangeKey, or pre-write readback differs from an explicitly supplied ETag.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact resource and compare observed ETag with the rejected precondition.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact resource again (same account and ID), compare the intervening changes, and issue a new update using the current @odata.etag/eTag. The refused request carried If-Match or failed the pre-write ETag comparison, so it was not applied.
  • Read the exact resource again and review its changed contents before requesting a new update with the new ETag.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate new edit uses the current version after reviewing intervening changes.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
